summary: Target-level continuation of the accepted A0-extension, narrowed to algebraic-space Weil restriction, comparison with ModularCurves finite quotients and moduli-specific descent compatibility. General spaces, atlases, quotient sheaves, products, properties and stack theory are imported from SF.1. Affine restriction, finite locally free and curve descent, and polarized etale scheme descent retain their existing owners. The 38 inherited module-descent nodes are cited rather than copied. Every narrowed target is planned; supplier and typed-interface refinements remain explicit, and no implementation is certified.

nodes.title: Relative morphisms from a finite source
nodes.statement: For scheme-representable f:Z→B and x:X→B, define Mor_B(Z,X)(T) to be pairs consisting of a point a in B(T) and a morphism b:T×_B Z→X satisfying x∘b=f∘pr_Z. Restriction along g:T′→T keeps a|T′ and precomposes b with the canonical fibre map. Retain the projection to B. The representing scheme of T×_B Z is a choice; replacing it gives a canonical natural isomorphism.
hypotheses: Fix a universe of schemes. All space carriers are the fppf sheaves and full subcategory supplied by SF.1; no second algebraic-space carrier is introduced.
The source f:Z→B is representable by schemes. This includes every finite locally free map of algebraic spaces.
proofSteps: Use native relative representability to choose the scheme Z_T and native Yoneda to store a point of B(T), not a large type of natural transformations.
Define restriction by the universal fibre map and prove the identity/composition equations.
Yoneda on each Z_T gives the evaluation equivalence; the pullback universal property determines the projection, extensionality and adjunction.

sources.match: The relative morphism functor retains the base point and a map from the base-changed source; the sheaf points on a space test have the same description.

acceptance: The universal property is natural in the test, source and target, and comparison for different representing choices preserves the actual morphism b.
The empty-source case is the terminal object over B, hence B as an absolute presheaf.

uses.how: An etale target atlas induces a covering of the relative morphism functor.
Weil restriction is the fibre of postcomposition at the identity of Z.

uses.where: R09.1 relative parameter spaces and R09.4 moduli Isom tests
uses.how: Finite-source morphisms must agree with the imported affine representing algebra rather than a new coordinate construction.

nodes.title: Etale spaces of sections over a finite source
nodes.statement: Let p:Z→U be finite locally free between schemes and w:W→Z etale, with W an algebraic space. The sheaf of sections of W_T→Z_T is an algebraic space etale over U. If w is surjective its projection to U is surjective in the etale topology. No separatedness of W→Z is required in the conclusion.
hypotheses: U and Z are schemes; p is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation.
W is an algebraic space, and w is etale; w is surjective only for the final assertion.
proofSteps: For separated etale W→Z, identify a section with its open and closed image inside W_T. Use the requested finite-part sheaf and the open locus where its map to Z_T is an isomorphism. For the finite open subspace Z′ of W_T, its map to T is flat and locally of finite presentation because it is open in W_T and W_T→Z_T→T has those properties; finiteness makes it universally closed. The target Z_T→T is finite, hence closed, separated and locally of finite type. These are exactly the hypotheses of 05XD.

For general W, choose a separated scheme etale atlas W′→W. Sections of W′ give a representable-by-spaces etale cover of the section sheaf: its fibre over a section is the separated case for W′_T×_{W_T}Z_T.
Surjectivity follows by splitting the finitely many source-fibre points after an etale neighbourhood of U (05XQ). Apply SF.1 Artin bootstrap and etale locality on the source.

sources.match: Finite source fibres allow local simultaneous lifts; separated section spaces are open in the finite-part sheaf, and a separated atlas removes the separatedness hypothesis.
The finite-part functor of a separated locally finite type morphism is an etale algebraic space.
The isomorphism locus is open with the stated flatness, finite-presentation, closure and separation hypotheses.

acceptance: The result is etale as a map of algebraic spaces, without asserting representability by schemes.
For p the identity it recovers W→U; for Z empty it is U; for a split rank-two source and a constant two-element etale fibre it has four sections.
The nonseparated step uses W′→Z separated, not the false claim that W→Z is separated.

nodes.title: Algebraicity of relative morphisms
nodes.statement: For algebraic spaces Z→B and X→B with Z→B finite locally free, Mor_B(Z,X) is an algebraic space. Its points and structural map are those of r093-relative-hom. There is no finite-presentation, separatedness, affineness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on X.
hypotheses: B, Z and X are algebraic spaces.
Z→B is finite locally free; finite flat alone without local finite presentation is not the convention.
proofSteps: The functor is an fppf sheaf by gluing the base map and then the relative morphism. Work etale locally on B to make B affine and Z finite free.

Choose an etale atlas X′→X that is a disjoint union of affine schemes. For a point represented by b:Z_T→X, the pullback of Mor_B(Z,X′)→Mor_B(Z,X) is the section space for Z_T×_X X′→Z_T; r093-etale-sections proves etale representability by spaces and surjectivity.

For a finite collection of atlas components the target disjoint union is affine; its relative morphism space is represented by the arbitrary-algebra affine restriction supplied by RG2.0a. Maps landing in that finite union form an open subfunctor: the complement projects closed under the finite map Z_T→T.

On affine scheme tests T the finite source Z_T is quasi-compact, so a finite collection of components suffices. These open pieces therefore cover as sheaves. Glue their representers and apply Artin bootstrap to the etale cover, then descend from the etale base chart. The atlas-component index and its finite subsets stay in the fixed universe; each arbitrary-generator affine representer also stays there. Thus the covering coproduct meets the same size bounds as the source proof, 05Y7 footnote 3, p.16; no unrestricted larger-universe atlas is silently assumed.

sources.match: The proof passes from an arbitrary affine-coordinate representing algebra through finite subcollections of an atlas and an etale cover of the functor.
The affine finite-source representing construction permits arbitrary sets of generators and relations, then glues over a finite locally free base.

acceptance: Do not reduce an arbitrary X to a finitely presented affine target. RG2.0a supplies the arbitrary algebra version; MC0F alone would be insufficient.
A source of rank zero gives B, and the rank-one identity case gives X.
Formation agrees on overlaps of base charts by the evaluation property, with identity and composition coherence.

nodes.title: Weil restriction as the sheaf of sections
nodes.statement: For scheme-representable f:Z→B and z:X→Z define Res_{Z/B}(X)(T) as pairs (a,b), with a in B(T) and b:T×_B Z→X satisfying z∘b=pr_Z. The map to B remembers a, and pullback of points uses the canonical fibre map. In the intended algebraic-space application f is finite locally free. This is a sections condition, stronger than the relative B-morphism condition.
hypotheses: Fix a universe of schemes. All space carriers are the fppf sheaves and full subcategory supplied by SF.1; no second algebraic-space carrier is introduced.
The source f:Z→B is representable by schemes. This includes every finite locally free map of algebraic spaces.
proofSteps: Use the chosen scheme representing Z_T and the native value of X on it. Enforce equality after applying z, not merely after composing z with f.
Transport along the canonical fibre maps and prove the functor and natural projection laws.
The universal property expresses the right adjoint to base change from objects over B to objects over Z; it also fixes choice comparison and postcomposition.

sources.match: Restriction parametrizes actual Z-sections on the base-changed source, with natural evaluation on space tests.

acceptance: The native suggested definition has the actual equality to pr_Z in its point subtype.
On a split source it retains one independent component for each source component.

uses.how: This is the functor whose algebraicity the stage supplies.

uses.where: R09.1 finite-source parameter comparisons; R09.4 moduli descent and AbelianSchemes A0 consumers
uses.how: Use sections over the finite cover, preserving the base map and all structure maps.
The universal evaluation identifies their affine representers with the space-valued extension.

nodes.title: The fppf sheaf property of restriction
nodes.statement: If B, Z and X are fppf sheaves and f:Z→B is scheme-representable, then Res_{Z/B}(X) is an fppf sheaf. Its evaluation universal property holds on every algebraic-space test. Finite local freeness is not required for this sheaf assertion.
hypotheses: X, Z and B satisfy the fppf sheaf condition.
Use the same native representing choices as r093-weil-restriction.
proofSteps: Glue the compatible base points in B. Pull the covering family back to Z_T and glue the local maps to X.
Check the equality with pr_Z after the cover using separatedness of Z as a sheaf, not separatedness as a morphism.
Choose an etale scheme presentation of a space test and apply the quotient sheaf universal property to extend the evaluation statement.

sources.match: Both the sheaf property and evaluation on algebraic-space tests use only sheaf gluing, not the finite-source representability argument.

acceptance: A proof may not add flatness or finite presentation to the target X.
The base and section maps are glued, not only isomorphism classes.

nodes.title: Arbitrary base change of Weil restriction
nodes.statement: For B′→B set Z′=B′×_B Z and X′=Z′×_Z X. There is a canonical isomorphism over B′ between Res_{Z′/B′}(X′) and B′×_B Res_{Z/B}(X). It carries (a′,b′) to the same section of Z_T, using the canonical associativity isomorphisms. It is natural in X, is the identity for identity base change and agrees with the composite for two base changes.
hypotheses: B′→B is any morphism of algebraic spaces, or of presheaves for the pointwise version.
f is scheme-representable, as is its base change. No finite local freeness is needed to identify the functors.
proofSteps: For T→B′ identify T×_{B′}Z′ with T×_B Z and maps into X′ over Z′ with maps into X over Z.
Give both inverse transformations explicitly and verify their pointwise roundtrips.
All naturality, unit and composition equations follow from preservation of the same section b and the uniqueness clause of the evaluation property.

sources.match: Restriction and the fibre product on the base have identical test-section descriptions.

acceptance: Test a nonflat B′→B, such as a residue field of a nonreduced base.
Compare MC0F and RG2.0a base-change maps on their common affine domains; identity/composition are equations of the canonical isomorphisms, not only existence.

nodes.title: Restriction is the identity fibre of relative morphisms
nodes.statement: Postcomposition with z:X→Z gives Mor_B(Z,X)→Mor_B(Z,Z), where X is viewed over B. The identity section of Z gives B→Mor_B(Z,Z). The resulting square with Res_{Z/B}(X), its inclusion into Mor_B(Z,X) and its projection to B is cartesian as presheaves and fppf sheaves. All four maps are fixed by evaluation, and the square is natural under arbitrary base change.
hypotheses: X→Z→B are morphisms of algebraic spaces with Z→B scheme-representable.
proofSteps: Evaluate the square at T. A point in its fibre product is a pair (a,b) whose composite z∘b equals the identity section on Z_T.
This is exactly the defining equality for restriction; build inverse transformations with the same a and b.
Use pointwise limits of presheaves and the fact that sheaf fibre products use these limits.

sources.match: The sections functor is the fibre at the identity of postcomposition on relative morphisms.

acceptance: Replacing the identity point by an arbitrary endomorphism would define a different fibre.
The cartesian comparison preserves the maps to B and the evaluation section.

nodes.title: Algebraic-space Weil restriction
nodes.statement: For morphisms X→Z→B of algebraic spaces, if Z→B is finite locally free, Res_{Z/B}(X) is an algebraic space. Its structural map, functorial evaluation and arbitrary-base-change comparison are the previously specified ones. No hypothesis of affineness, finite presentation, separatedness or quasi-compactness is imposed on X.
hypotheses: Z→B is finite locally free; it need not be surjective and may have rank zero on components.
proofSteps: Apply algebraicity of relative morphisms to Mor_B(Z,X) and Mor_B(Z,Z).
Use r093-restriction-cartesian and closure of algebraic spaces under fibre products.
Identify the represented sheaf with r093-weil-restriction by the specified evaluation map, then carry base change across that identification.

sources.match: Finite locally free restriction is algebraic because it is a fibre product of the two algebraic relative morphism spaces.

acceptance: The result is an algebraic space; it does not claim it is a scheme or has arbitrary desirable morphism properties.
Identity, terminal, empty and split-rank-two tests agree with the defining functor.
Restriction of an etale target map is etale as a map of spaces (05YD), with surjectivity when the target map is surjective; this reduces to the section-space theorem.

nodes.title: Compatibility with the existing affine restriction
nodes.statement: On MC0F’s domain (Z/B finite locally free schemes and X/Z affine finitely presented), the MC0F representing scheme, embedded into SF.1 algebraic spaces, is canonically isomorphic over B to r093-restriction-algebraicity. On the affine-base arbitrary-algebra domain of RG2.0a the same comparison uses its representing algebra. Both are determined by the common map b:Z_T→X. The comparisons agree where both suppliers apply, preserve target morphisms and commute with all base-change maps and their unit/composition equations.
hypotheses: Retain each supplier’s stated hypotheses.
For the unrestricted affine coordinate reduction use the arbitrary-algebra representing-algebra node of RG2.0a, not only MC0F’s finitely presented case.
proofSteps: Read the two representing properties as natural bijections into the same test-section set.
Compose the bijections to construct the unique Yoneda isomorphism preserving the evaluation section.
Prove the overlap and base-change equations by evaluation uniqueness; preserve Spec contravariance when comparing the ring-side adjunction.

sources.locator: Layer 0F, affine Weil restriction paragraph (Markdown; no page numbering)
sources.match: This existing target represents the affine finitely presented functor and already supplies arbitrary base change.
The comparison is forced by the section-valued representing property.
The unrestricted affine functor is the same arbitrary-generator coordinate problem assigned to RG2.0a.

acceptance: There is no newly planned affine coordinate algebra or torus splitting theorem in this packet.
Check the comparison for a split two-point finite source and for a rank-zero source.
An inverse system of affine targets of unbounded presentation is not forced into the MC0F finitely presented interface.

nodes.title: Compatibility of effective finite quotients
nodes.statement: Let R⇉U be an equivalence relation of schemes in MC0C’s affine or invariant-affine-cover effective finite locally free quotient domain. Let q:U→Q_MC be its supplied quotient, with q faithfully flat locally of finite presentation and R≅U×_{Q_MC}U. The SF.1 fppf quotient sheaf U/R is canonically h_{Q_MC}, with the same map from U. This is natural for maps of effective relations and commutes with base changes for which the MC0C construction applies. When s,t are also etale this identifies the SF.1 etale-relation quotient. For a free finite constant group action with the required invariant affine cover it identifies the torsor quotient. No such sheaf-quotient comparison is asserted for actions with stabilizers.
hypotheses: The relation is effective, with its actual kernel-pair identification and fppf cover q, as supplied by MC0C.
General finite locally free relations need not be etale. The comparison uses the fppf quotient sheaf and the existing MC0C scheme, not the etale quotient theorem alone.
proofSteps: The fppf cover q is locally surjective as a sheaf map and its kernel pair is h_R. Thus h_Q is the coequalizer sheaf of h_R⇉h_U.
Use the SF.1 quotient-sheaf universal property to obtain the unique isomorphism preserving q.
Morphisms of relations and allowed base changes commute by this uniqueness; on the etale subdomain use the same coequalizer to identify the etale quotient.

sources.locator: Layer 0C, finite quotients and torsors (Markdown; no page numbering)
sources.match: MC0C owns the effective finite locally free scheme quotient and free-action specializations.

sources.locator: §9, Lemma 9.1 (0262), p.12, presentation by a quotient sheaf
sources.match: For an etale presentation the quotient is the coequalizer of its kernel pair; this identifies the etale specialization of the comparison.

The supplied scheme represents the fppf quotient sheaf when its projection is locally surjective and its kernel-pair relation agrees with the supplied relation. This criterion does not require etale relation projections.

acceptance: For U=B disjoint union B with its full effective relation, the quotient is B and both comparison routes preserve the fold map.
A free constant C2 action on its split two-point torsor gives the same quotient B.

Reject the nonfree sign action on A1 over a characteristic-zero field: over dual numbers the points x=0 and x=epsilon have the same invariant x²=0 but are never locally in the same C2 orbit. Faithful flatness keeps epsilon nonzero. The invariant-ring quotient cannot be substituted for the fppf orbit sheaf.

nodes.title: Coherent descent along an etale presentation
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space, U→X an etale surjective scheme presentation and R=U×_X U with source and target s,t. Restriction induces an equivalence between coherent O_X-modules and pairs consisting of a coherent module M on U and an isomorphism t* M≅s* M satisfying the diagonal and triple-overlap equations. Morphisms are all module maps commuting with this isomorphism, including zero and noninvertible maps. The equivalence is exact, independent of the presentation, and natural under base changes X′→X for which X′ is locally Noetherian. Invertible modules give the rank-one restriction of the inherited finite locally free equivalence.
hypotheses: X is locally Noetherian in the sense that one, hence every, etale scheme atlas is locally Noetherian.
Coherent means the existing small-etale-site module notion; on this class it equals quasi-coherent finite type and quasi-coherent finite presentation.
No claim of coherence under arbitrary change to a non-Noetherian target is made. Finite presentation, not coherent terminology, is the invariant used there.
proofSteps: Use the SF.1 equivalence between QCoh(X) and modules on the etale presentation, and the inherited full fpqc descent comparison; do not rebuild quasi-coherent descent. Use the fpqc cover and U×_X X_i in step 4 of 04W8, as corrected in the predecessor’s source issue AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/E4; the printed fppf label does not strengthen an arbitrary fpqc cover.
Apply 07UB on the locally Noetherian charts. Finite presentation descends by the inherited finite-presentation theorem, so the equivalence restricts to coherent objects in both directions.
Etale pullback is exact, and the coherent category is abelian (07UC). The equivalence therefore preserves kernels and cokernels.

Use a common refinement of two presentations; full faithfulness fixes its natural comparisons and the triple-refinement coherence. Base change preserves finite presentation, and 07UB identifies coherence when the new space is locally Noetherian.

sources.match: Quasi-coherent descent includes all maps; finite presentation and finite local freeness can be checked after the cover.
On a locally Noetherian space, coherence is equivalent to quasi-coherent finite presentation on every or one etale chart, and coherent modules form an abelian category.

acceptance: On a scheme presentation this agrees with the existing Zariski module carrier; no second coherent-sheaf definition is introduced.
Check the identity presentation, refinement by two identical chart copies, and descent of a noninvertible map such as multiplication by a parameter on an affine Noetherian chart.
This supplies coherent etale descent for downstream analytic comparison; proper GAGA remains owned by ComplexComparisonPartII C3 and is not a prerequisite here.

nodes.title: Comparison of descended polarized objects
nodes.statement: For an fppf cover S′→S of schemes, let Y′→S′ be proper finitely presented with a relatively ample invertible sheaf L′. Give an isomorphism of Y′ over S′×_S S′ satisfying the identity and triple cocycle, and a specified lift identifying the two pullbacks of L′ satisfying its own identity and triple cocycle. The general SF.1 polarized-object descent supplier gives (Y,L) over S with an identification of the pullback pair with (Y′,L′). On the domain of MC0E polarized projective relative curves or SR Layer 2 etale polarized schemes, their supplied descended pair is uniquely isomorphic to this pair by an isomorphism whose pullback is the specified identity. These comparisons preserve polarized morphisms and sections, and satisfy refinement and arbitrary-base-change coherence. The line-bundle cocycle is data, not inferred from invariance of an isomorphism class of L′.
hypotheses: The base cover is fppf; all object and line-bundle cocycle identifications are supplied explicitly.
The pair is proper finitely presented and relatively polarized. Projectivity is asserted in the supplier’s local-on-base convention, with relatively ample L and properness.
For SR comparison the cover is etale; for MC0E comparison the object is a relative curve in MC0E’s stated class.
proofSteps: Import descent of the underlying algebraic space from SF.1 and invertible-module descent from its quasi-coherent presentation interface. Descend the specified lift of the object cocycle to L′.

The requested SF.1 polarized-object theorem uses fpqc locality of relative ampleness (0D3C) to make the descended space a scheme over S; properness and finite presentation descend independently. R09.3 does not plan this general theorem again.

Full faithfulness of object and module descent gives the unique comparison between any two descended pairs with the given local identity; it preserves the polarization map and all compatible morphisms and sections.
Pull back the local identity under refinement or base change. Uniqueness identifies the resulting comparison with the directly constructed one, giving unit and composition coherence.

sources.match: Ampleness descends fpqc locally, and the proof recovers a scheme from the descended section algebra; the descent datum first gives a sheaf (0ADT), and SF.1 supplies its algebraicity; the invertible sheaf has a separate descent input.

sources.locator: Layer 0E, effective descent of polarized projective relative curves
sources.match: The curve case is already owned by ModularCurves.

sources.locator: Layer 2, effective etale descent of polarized schemes
sources.match: StableReduction owns the etale scheme case, including morphisms, sections and multiplication.

acceptance: Changing the line-bundle cocycle by units is allowed to change the descended bundle; comparison requires the actual cocycle, not merely an invariant Picard class.

The identity cover gives the original polarized pair. For a split two-sheet cover the componentwise identity cocycle gives the original pair and componentwise nontrivial transition units are retained.
Do not assert effectiveness of arbitrary scheme descent or a projective object from line-bundle descent alone.

nodes.title: Compatibility of descent with finite moduli data
nodes.statement: For an fppf cover S′→S and a finite locally free group scheme G′/S′ with descent datum by group isomorphisms, import MC0E’s descended finite locally free group G/S. If one also supplies a compatible finite locally free closed subgroup H′→G′, a compatible torsor under G′, and a finite tuple of compatible sections and morphisms of these objects satisfying specified equations, compare the simultaneous MC0E descent with SF.1 space and quasi-coherent descent. There is a unique isomorphism of the descended tuples preserving the specified local identifications, the group operations, subgroup immersion, torsor action, sections and all the equations. It commutes coherently with arbitrary base change and with forgetting any of the extra data. This stage supplies the comparison, not a second construction of any finite flat group or level-structure moduli scheme.
hypotheses: Every scheme declared finite locally free is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation over its base.
Descent isomorphisms commute with the multiplication, identity, inverse and all supplied structure maps; the triple cocycle is part of the datum.
A torsor uses the imported fppf torsor definition; a subgroup includes its actual closed immersion. No abelian dual or polarizing isogeny is introduced here.
proofSteps: Use MC0E for the existing group, subgroup, torsor and section descent. View these schemes through SF.1’s fully faithful scheme embedding.
The SF.1 descended spaces agree with these schemes by full faithfulness of descent. Transport the operations and maps through the unique isomorphisms.

Check every equation on the fppf cover, where the comparison is the identity; faithfulness reflects it globally. For subgroup properties and finite local freeness use their supplied descent interfaces.
The same local-identity characterization proves compatibility with forgetting data and arbitrary base change.

sources.locator: Layer 0E, descent of finite locally free schemes, groups, torsors, subgroups and level structures
sources.match: All the effective finite moduli descent constructions are already assigned to this supplier.

Full module descent and descent of finite local freeness identify the module construction routes. Lemma 23.1 identifies a space datum with an fppf sheaf; the separate SF.1 space-descent theorem supplies effectivity, and full faithfulness reflects all structure equations.

acceptance: Use a split two-sheet cover to check that the comparison retains the specified multiplication and marked sections, rather than only the underlying finite scheme.
Check identity subgroup, trivial group and the translation action on the trivial torsor.
An incompatible local section is not descended. Abelian polarization representability remains with the downstream abelian-scheme and moduli-stage owners.

coverage.detail: All narrowed targets are covered by 13 new target-level nodes, existing SF.1 imports and the 38 accepted predecessor nodes. General spaces and stacks, affine restriction, effective finite quotient construction and standard module/finite-object descent retain their existing owners. Mathematical planning is complete; the explicit supplier requests and interface refinements prevent closure.
remaining: Discharge the two exact SF.1 extensions for section spaces and general fppf polarized objects.
Complete the three concrete supplier signatures recorded in the suggested-file comments and verify them against the single common space/module carriers.
Reconcile and implement the inherited native module adapters without creating another quasi-coherent descent theory; transport the comonad structure and comparison functor explicitly.
Implement the specified maps and comparisons and discharge their proofs; successful signature elaboration and acceptance of this plan establish neither implementation nor signature completeness.

requests.need: The already planned affine finitely presented Weil-restriction representer, its section-valued universal property and arbitrary-base-change comparison. Import it unchanged.

The already planned affine/invariant-affine effective finite locally free scheme quotient with its fppf projection, kernel-pair identification and universal map; free constant-group torsor specialization.

The existing full descent functors for affine and finite locally free schemes, group objects, subgroups, torsors, sections and polarized projective relative curves, with their given local identification and base-change coherence.

The existing etale descent equivalence of schemes with a specified relatively ample invertible sheaf, including polarized morphisms, sections and coherence of the section algebra/relative Proj construction.

Supply the missing general etale-space tools used by the sections proof: for separated locally finite type W→U the finite-part sheaf of open subspaces of W_T finite over T is an etale algebraic space (04QH); and the open isomorphism-locus theorem 05XD with its exact hypotheses. These are additions to the common space-property interface, not an independent R09.3 space carrier.

Extend the general space/module descent interface to fppf descent of proper finitely presented schemes with a specified relatively ample invertible sheaf and a lifted cocycle. Include all polarized morphisms, sections and arbitrary-base-change/refinement coherence; recover the scheme using 0D3C. Existing galois-descent-quasi-projective is only the finite-locally-free base-cover case. MC0E and SR retain their narrower existing implementations.

gaps.title: The finite-part and open-isomorphism interfaces have no exact SF.1 node
gaps.detail: The source proof of 05XR is read and the argument is specified, but its 04QH and 05XD interfaces are neither in the pinned libraries nor exact existing SF.1 nodes. The stage request names them and their hypotheses. The relative-Hom and Weil algebraicity targets depend on this request; they are planned, not closed.

gaps.title: General fppf polarized-object descent needs the SF.1 extension
gaps.detail: MC0E covers polarized relative curves and SR covers etale polarized schemes. Neither supplies general fppf proper polarized schemes. The exact SF.1 request is required for the comparison on that broader domain; no such theorem is assumed from either special case.

gaps.title: Inherited chosen-pullback module adapters remain proof obligations
gaps.detail: The accepted A0-extension’s 38 R09.3 nodes remain unchanged and unchecked. Its extension-coordinate, diagonal/triple, chosen-overlap equivalence, native canonical comparison, equalizer/counit and comonadic-adjunction transport signatures must be reconciled with SF.1/qcoh-pseudofunctor and qcoh-fpqc-descent. Native rightAdjointUniq and its unit/counit equations are read and prototyped here as existing library inputs, not new roadmap targets. An equivalence of coalgebras must transport comultiplication and the canonical comparison, not merely supply a natural isomorphism of right functors. Coherent descent consumes the inherited full descent and finite-presentation nodes, so it cannot certify their proofs.

gaps.title: Concrete supplier signatures are pending common carrier implementation
gaps.detail: The suggested file gives both native small-presheaf definitions, all 20 API items and seven tests, the sheaf/diagonal/atlas algebraicity conditions and the etale-section signature, plus native evaluation and quotient universal properties for affine and finite-quotient comparisons. Three concrete signatures still require supplier declarations absent at the pins: the small-etale coherent-space equivalence, polarized-pair comparison and finite-structured MC0E/SF.1 comparison. Their exact full mathematical signatures are recorded under their proposed names in comments, never fabricated Prop fields. Elaboration does not certify these omitted signatures or any proofs.

restructure.proposal: Apply the confirmed RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/1 ownership: SF.1 supplies all general algebraic-space, atlas, quotient-sheaf, product, morphism-property and stack foundations to R09.3. Retain here the finite-source space restriction extension, comparison with MC0C quotients, coherent presentation descent specialization and comparisons of moduli-specific data. upstreamNotes.note: Current main includes AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A/L0B, absent from the atlas snapshot. It owns module pullback, its monoidal/coherence API, quasi-coherent and finite locally free wrappers, and L1 relative Spec. Current TauCeti at a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039 implements Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_pullback, isFinitePresentation_pullback, pullbackObjUnitIso and restrictPullbackObjIso in Modules/Pullback/Basic.lean and affine tensor comparisons in Pullback/Affine.lean. These do not replace general fpqc descent, but the inherited pullback nodes must consume them when rebased.

Current TauCeti Quotient/Affine.lean and Quotient/FiniteGroup/Affine.lean implement invariant-ring spectrum quotients and affine-target universality, with integrality/finiteness results. They do not provide the effective fppf relation quotient used in the comparison. An action with stabilizers must not be identified with its fppf orbit sheaf from this library API alone.

The predecessor coverage mentions proper GAGA. It is a downstream ComplexComparisonPartII C3 result, not an R09.3 prerequisite. This stage exports coherent etale presentation descent. R09.2 retains proper modifications and Chow/coherent devissage; no analytic or projective parameter-space construction is added here.

Confirmed finding /12 is handled at the boundary: R09.1 should import MC0G Grassmannians and SR Layer 2 relative Proj/ampleness. This issue changes no R09.1 deliverable. R09.3 imports the same polarization APIs for comparisons and introduces no new Grassmannian or relative Proj.

review.notes: Independent review of all 13 new targets, all 19 pinned baseline declarations, all supplier contracts, 20 definition API entries, seven suggested tests, six planets, eight hash-matched public source PDFs, three source misprints and confirmed findings /1, /10, /11, /12. Corrected three baseline declaration kinds, added two evaluation-characterisation API signatures, made section-locus hypotheses and atlas size explicit, carried forward predecessor E4 and removed the completed review from remaining work. Suggested Lean elaborates with only the expected admitted-proof warnings. Accepted as a complete target-planning pass; R09.3 stays planned, not closed, with four explicit supplier/interface/proof gaps. No nodes, proofs or inherited adapters are certified implemented.
